persona: Friendly and a bit embarrassed. Calls it 'house insurance'. Lost the original receipt when moving house, so asked the store for a copy the day after the accident.
initial_message: Hi, I need to claim on my house insurance. I knocked my TV off its stand while moving the couch on Monday night (28 Sept) and the screen is smashed.

facts.incident.description: I was pushing the couch back against the wall, my foot caught the TV power cable and the TV toppled off its stand. It landed on its top left corner. Afterwards I stood it up on its feet on the carpet in front of the cabinet.
facts.incident.cause: Accidentally pulled off the stand by the power cable
facts.loss.description: 65-inch TV screen shattered from the top left corner
facts.contents.receipt_availability: A reprint of the receipt from the store, available now. The original was lost when I moved house.
facts.policyholder.name: Sione Talavale
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the broken screen. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: Receipt reprint from Longreach Tech Store, printed on 29 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_dates: I bought the TV on 14 November 2025. The store printed this copy for me on 29 September because I lost the original.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in a living room at night. A large 65-inch widescreen television has toppled off an empty low wooden TV cabinet and is propped up on the beige carpet in front of it, leaning back on its two slim metal feet, one at each end of the bottom edge. A TV remote control lies on the carpet beside it and a sofa arm is at the edge of the frame. The top of the cabinet is empty. The glass screen is shattered in a spider-web of cracks spreading from the top left corner, with dark ink blotches under the glass. The thin black border has no markings. Warm lamp light. No logo, no text, no people.
materials.design_note: The 0.2 close-up (seed 422001) was read by gpt-4o, image only, as a broken glass table. This frame shows the whole TV, its feet and a remote; gpt-4o reads it as a television. Seeds 422101-422103 and 422201-422203 were rejected: a round monitor-style base, or a second TV in the room.

design.notes: Innocent control: the reprint date (29 September 2026) is after the accident, the purchase date (14 November 2025) is not. Only the purchase date counts (rules, section 3).

triage.rationale: Accidental damage at the insured address, nobody hurt, photo and proof of purchase supplied, one item at NZD 1,499, policy on file. The receipt reprint date (29 September) is after the accident, but only the purchase date (14 November 2025) counts. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system). It also assumes a receipt counts as proof of ownership.

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 14 November 2025 is before the incident; the reprint date 29 September 2026 is ignored

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 January 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2022-11-05, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
